Executable: /workspace/dataset/test12_executable
Source (Python, for reference):
    import argparse
    from furl import furl
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--d', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    f = furl(args.a)
    print(f.fragment.__setattr__('str', args.b) or f.fragment)   # LINE1
    print(f.fragment.add(args.c))                                # LINE2
    print(f.fragment.set(args.d, 'value'))                       # LINE3
    print(f.url)                                                 # LINE4

RUN IT LIKE: /workspace/dataset/test12_executable --a "<A>" --b "<B>" --c "<C>" --d "<D>"
Never use the 'python' command. Do not read furl source; it is not available. Probe empirically.

ALREADY-ESTABLISHED FACTS (do not re-derive, but DO stress-test if in your area):
- --b is completely ignored: __setattr__('str', b) sets a dead instance attribute, no effect, returns None.
- LINE1 prints str(fragment) as parsed from A.
- LINE2 = fragment.path.add(C) then print str(fragment).
- LINE3 = fragment.path.load(D); fragment.query.load('value'); print str(fragment)  -> query is always literally 'value'.
- LINE4 prints the whole URL with the mutated fragment.
- Fragment str = path + '?' + query when both non-empty, else path+query. When query non-empty, literal '?' chars inside the fragment PATH are escaped to %3F; when query is empty they stay raw.
- furl DECODES percent-escapes on parse and RE-ENCODES on output: '%41%42' -> 'AB'; '%2F' inside a path segment -> stays '%2F'; lone '%' -> '%25'; 'a%zz' -> 'a%25zz'.
- Scheme and host are lowercased. Default ports dropped (http:80, https:443) but non-default kept (http:443 kept).
- URL query: '+' decodes to space, space encodes to '+'. 'a=b&c&d=' round-trips exactly (key-only 'c' vs empty-value 'd=' are distinct).

METHOD: run MANY probes (60+), vary one thing at a time, use printf %q or cat -A style to make whitespace visible, and note exit codes and stderr separately. Prefer a bash loop over a case list.

DELIVERABLE: a precise, implementable specification of YOUR assigned area: exact algorithm/rules, character sets (list the literal safe characters), ordering of operations, and a table of at least 25 concrete input->output examples you actually observed (verbatim). Call out anything surprising or that you could not determine. Be rigorous: an implementer will code directly from your spec with no access to the executable.


AREA UNDER AUDIT: url-path

Another agent produced these RULES for this area:
R1. SCOPE: LINE4 = str(furl(A).url) with only the fragment mutated. The main path is untouched by --b/--c/--d; those only affect the fragment. Verified: A='http://ex.com/a b' with --c 'Q Q' --d 'ZZ' still yields path '/a%20b'.
R2. STEP 0 (pre-parse sanitization): Before any parsing, ALL occurrences of the bytes TAB (0x09), LF (0x0A) and CR (0x0D) are deleted from the entire raw URL string. This is Python urlsplit behavior and happens before percent-decoding, so it can splice a broken escape back together: 'x%2<TAB>0y' -> 'x%20y' -> decodes to 'x y' -> re-encodes to 'x%20y'. VT (0x0B) and FF (0x0C) are NOT stripped (they become %0B / %0C).
R3. STEP 1 (delimiting): The path is the substring after the netloc and before the FIRST raw '#' or the FIRST raw '?', whichever comes first. Raw '#' and raw '?' can never appear in the path; only their percent-encoded forms %23 / %3F can.
R4. STEP 2 (split): Split the RAW (still percent-encoded) path string on the literal character '/'. Splitting happens BEFORE percent-decoding. This is the decisive ordering fact: 'a%2Fb' stays ONE segment and prints back as 'a%2Fb'; 'a/b' is TWO segments. Encoded slashes never create segment boundaries.
R5. STEP 3 (decode, per segment): For each segment independently, percent-decode. Decoding is a SINGLE pass over the raw bytes: scan left to right; on '%' followed by two hex digits (either case) emit that byte and advance 3; otherwise emit the '%' (or current byte) literally and advance 1. Therefore '%2525' -> the 4-char text '%25' -> re-encodes to '%2525' (idempotent, no double decode). '%25%32%46' -> text '%2F' -> re-encodes to '%252F'.
R6. STEP 3a (invalid escapes): A '%' not followed by two hex digits is kept as a literal '%' character: 'a%' -> text 'a%', 'a%z' -> 'a%z', 'a%zz' -> 'a%zz', 'a%4' -> 'a%4', '%%41' -> '%A' (first '%' is literal because '%4' is not two hex digits... observed output '%25%2541' shows the decoded text is literally '%' + '%41' i.e. the second escape is ALSO not decoded). Concretely observed: input '%%41' -> output '%25%2541', i.e. decoded text is the 4-char string '%%41' with NO decoding at all of the '%41' part. Implementation that reproduces this: the scanner, upon seeing '%' not followed by 2 hex digits, emits '%' and advances by 1, then sees '%41' and WOULD decode it — that contradicts the output. The actual observed behavior is equivalent to: split on '%', and only treat a '%' as an escape if the two chars after it are hex; here '%' at index 0 is followed by '%4' (not hex) so literal, and the next '%41' is... see UNCERTAINTIES. Safest reproduction: use Python urllib.parse.unquote semantics on the byte string, which yields '%%41' unchanged for this input.
R7. STEP 3b (byte->text): The decoded byte sequence is interpreted as UTF-8 with errors='replace'. Any byte or truncated/overlong/surrogate sequence that is not valid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD, one U+FFFD per undecodable byte. All 128 single bytes %80..%FF each produce exactly one U+FFFD (verified for every value 0x80-0xFF). '%ED%A0%80' (UTF-16 surrogate) -> 3x U+FFFD. '%C0%80' -> 2x U+FFFD. '%E4%B8' (truncated) -> 1x U+FFFD (the two bytes collapse to one replacement). '%E4x' -> U+FFFD + 'x'. Valid sequences decode normally: '%E4%B8%AD' -> U+4E2D, '%F0%9F%98%80' -> U+1F600.
R8. STEP 4 (encode, per segment): Re-encode each decoded segment. Encode the text as UTF-8, then for each byte: if the byte is one of the SAFE characters, emit it literally; otherwise emit '%' + two UPPERCASE hex digits. Hex output is ALWAYS uppercase regardless of input case ('%2f' -> '%2F', '%3c' -> '%3C', '%ff' -> '%EF%BF%BD').
R9. STEP 5 (rejoin): Join the re-encoded segments with '/'. Structure is preserved exactly: number of segments, empty segments, leading and trailing slashes are all kept verbatim.
R10. NO NORMALIZATION whatsoever: '.' and '..' segments are preserved literally ('/a/../b' -> '/a/../b', '/./a' -> '/./a', '/..' -> '/..'). Empty segments preserved ('/a//b' -> '/a//b', '//a' -> '//a', '///a' -> '///a', '/a//' -> '/a//'). A path of exactly '/' stays '/'. An absent path stays absent ('http://ex.com' -> 'http://ex.com'). No length limit observed (300-char segment round-trips verbatim).
R11. NO path-parameter handling: ';' is an ordinary safe character. '/a;b=c;e/d' round-trips unchanged; the ';'-params are NOT split off or re-ordered.
R12. '+' is NOT special in the main path (unlike the query): raw '+' stays '+', and '%2B' DECODES to '+' and is re-emitted as literal '+'. So '%20%2B%2b+b' -> '%20+++b'. This is lossy/aliasing: '%2B' and '+' are indistinguishable after a round-trip.
R13. Case is preserved in the path (only scheme and host are lowercased): 'HTTP://Ex.CoM/PaTh%41/Zz' -> 'http://ex.com/PaThA/Zz'.
R14. The safe set is identical for every segment, including the first segment of a rootless relative path: 'a%3Ab/c' -> 'a:b/c' (':' is NOT escaped to disambiguate a scheme).
R15. Encoded delimiters survive: %23 -> '%23', %2F -> '%2F', %3F -> '%3F', %25 -> '%25'. They are decoded to '#', '/', '?', '%' internally and then re-encoded because those four characters are not in the safe set.
R16. The safe set does NOT change based on whether a query or fragment is present (unlike the fragment path, where '?' escaping is conditional). 'http://ex.com/x%3Fy?q=1' -> '/x%3Fy?q=1' and 'http://ex.com/x%23y?q=1' -> '/x%23y?q=1'.
R17. Raw non-ASCII input is read as UTF-8 from argv and encoded byte-wise: raw 'é' -> '%C3%A9', raw '中' -> '%E4%B8%AD'.
R18. Reference implementation of the safe test: SAFE = set(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~" + "!$&'()*+,;=" + ":@"). This is exactly RFC 3986 'pchar' = unreserved / sub-delims / ':' / '@'. Equivalently urllib.parse.quote(seg, safe="!$&'()*+,;=:@~") over the UTF-8 bytes.

And reported safe characters: "Left literal (unencoded) in a main-URL path segment — exactly 79 characters, the RFC 3986 pchar set: A-Z (26), a-z (26), 0-9 (10), and the punctuation ! $ & ' ( ) * + , - . : ; = @ _ ~   (17 punctuation chars). Percent-encoded to uppercase %XX: everything else, i.e. space, \" # % / < > ? [ \\ ] ^ ` { | } , all C0 controls 0x00-0x1F, DEL 0x7F, and every non-ASCII codepoint (as its UTF-8 bytes). Note '/' is only encoded when it is INSIDE a segment (i.e. arrived as %2F); as a raw input character it is the segment separator and stays raw."

YOUR JOB: adversarially falsify. For EACH rule, design at least one probe whose outcome the rule predicts, run it against the executable, and compare prediction vs actual. Default to reporting a rule as WRONG or INCOMPLETE if you find any input where it mispredicts. Also hunt for behavior the rules omit entirely (edge cases they never mention). Run at least 50 probes. Return corrections with verbatim observed outputs.

corrections.why:
There is no left-to-right scanner. For each segment furl first tests whether the segment is *already a well-formed encoded path segment*. If YES it percent-decodes it and re-encodes it. If NO it does not decode at all -- it just percent-encodes the raw segment (so every '%' becomes '%25'). A single defect anywhere in the segment suppresses decoding of ALL escapes in that segment, including perfectly valid ones far away. R5's scanner predicts '%zz%41' -> text '%zzA' -> output '%25zzA'; actual output is '%25zz%2541'. The real algorithm (validated by 1200 randomized differential probes, 0 mismatches) is:

SAFE = A-Za-z0-9 ! $ & ' ( ) * + , - . : ; = @ _ ~   (the 79 chars already documented).
VALID(seg) is true iff seg can be consumed entirely by repeating: (a) a char in SAFE, or (b) a non-ASCII codepoint that is a Python \w character, i.e. Unicode category L* / Nd / Nl / No (equivalently str.isalnum()), or (c) '%' followed by exactly two hex digits (either case).
For each raw segment s (after splitting the raw path on '/'):
    out = quote_utf8(unquote_utf8_replace(s))   if VALID(s)
    out = quote_utf8(s)                          if not VALID(s)
where quote_utf8 = encode text as UTF-8 then %XX-escape every byte not in SAFE (uppercase hex), and unquote_utf8_replace = replace every %XX with its byte, keep every other char's UTF-8 bytes, then decode the byte string as UTF-8 with errors='replace'.
Note the not-VALID branch is a plain SINGLE encode of the raw text (furl internally does quote() then unquote() then quote() again, but the middle pair cancels exactly).
